statement: `systems_to_json` writes the systems in order, the first the reference, as a dict whose `models` key lists each one's `system_to_json` document. Systems sharing a System id are refused.
reason: Each document is its own save, so the single-system format and its schema version stay as they are, and the file needs no version of its own. Refused: renaming a colliding System, which would hide which system is which.
sites: added efootprint/api_utils/system_to_json.py in systems_to_json — Refuses systems sharing a System id, naming it and duplicate_system; writes each one's `system_to_json`, in order, under the models key, to any file given.
tests: unit tests/api_utils_tests/test_system_to_json.py — `systems_to_json` writes the dict it returns to the file it is given
narrative tests/narratives/test_system_file.py — `systems_to_json` refuses two systems sharing a System id, naming the id and duplicate_system [distinct-systems]

statement: `load_systems` returns a comparison file's systems in the file's order, each loaded from its document by `load_system_document`.
reason: Systems alone are returned: a modeler compares systems, and each one reaches its objects. Two documents sharing a System id are not checked: only a file assembled by hand can, and their loads give separate objects. A single-system file given to the load fails with a KeyError on `models`: the mix-up gets no check of its own.
sites: added efootprint/api_utils/json_to_system.py in json_to_systems — Loads each document under the models key through `json_to_system`, in order, and returns their systems.
tests: narrative tests/narratives/test_system_file.py — systems written by `systems_to_json` come back from `load_systems` in their order, each as its own save and load gives it [round-trip]

waivers: any-count — Both functions walk the list and neither counts it, so no limit can be reached.
each-is-a-system-file — Each element of the list is what `system_to_json` returns for its system, unchanged.
old-files-upgrade — The load hands each document to `load_system_document`, whose earlier-version case of the save-and-load narrative holds the upgrade and the baseline.

lots: comparison-file (easy) #export #load — Two new functions of a few lines each, whose design the plan leaves nothing open in, and no existing code changes. #export is committed first: the round-trip case of #load writes its file with `systems_to_json`.
